title: Candidate metabolites in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: Network analysis and in vitro validation of glycitein.
authors: Hong, Yinghui; Ye, Mingliang; Huang, Bin; Li, Xi; Huang, Lei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究脓毒症相关脑病的代谢物网络分析与体外验证，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe neurological complication of sepsis. Cerebrovascular endothelial injury serves as a key contributor to its pathogenesis, and metabolite-mediated inflammatory regulation may be involved in this process. However, the specific candidate metabolites and their underlying pathways remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to identify candidate metabolites related to SAE through network pharmacology and to provide preliminary in vitro validation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A "microbiota-substrate-metabolite-target-signal pathway" (MMTS) network was constructed by integrating metabolite databases, target prediction resources, and sepsis-related encephalopathy gene databases. Candidate metabolites were screened through protein-protein interaction analysis, Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses, drug-likeness assessment, toxicology screening, and molecular docking. Glycitein was selected as a representative candidate for preliminary validation in a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced human brain microvascular endothelial cell (hCMEC/D3) injury model. Cell activity, migration, tube formation, inflammatory factor release, intracellular reactive oxygen species levels, and NF-kappaB-related molecule expression were assessed. RESULTS: A total of 206 gut microbiota-related metabolites and 1518 potential targets were identified. Network analysis predicted 20 key targets related to SAE. PPI network analysis indicated TNF, IL6, CXCL8, NFKB1, and TLR4 as central nodes. KEGG analysis was particularly enriched in the Toll-like receptor, NOD-like receptor, and NF-kappaB signaling. 14 candidate metabolites were retained after integrated screening. In LPS-treated hCMEC/D3 cells, glycitein partially restored cell viability, migration, and tube formation, reduced IL-6 and TNF-alpha levels, alleviated intracellular ROS accumulation, and was associated with downregulation of NFKB1, CXCL8, and IL-6 expression, together with reduced phosphorylation of NF-kappaB p65 and IkappaBalpha. CONCLUSIONS: This study prioritized candidate metabolites associated with SAE through database-supported network analysis. Preliminary in vitro validation suggested that glycitein was associated with attenuation of inflammatory endothelial injury-related phenotypes, providing a basis for further mechanistic studies.
abstract_zh: 背景：脓毒症相关性脑病（SAE）是脓毒症的一种严重神经系统并发症。脑血管内皮损伤是其发病机制中的关键因素，而代谢物介导的炎症调控可能参与该过程。然而，具体候选代谢物及其潜在通路仍缺乏明确表征。本研究旨在通过网络药理学识别与SAE相关的候选代谢物，并提供初步的体外验证。材料与方法：通过整合代谢物数据库、靶点预测资源及脓毒症相关性脑病基因数据库，构建了“微生物群-底物-代谢物-靶点-信号通路”（MMTS）网络。通过蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用分析、基因本体论及京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）富集分析、药物相似性评估、毒理学筛选和分子对接，筛选候选代谢物。选择大豆黄酮（glycitein）作为代表性候选物，在脂多糖（LPS）诱导的人脑微血管内皮细胞（hCMEC/D3）损伤模型中进行初步验证。评估了细胞活性、迁移、管形成、炎症因子释放、细胞内活性氧水平及NF-κB相关分子表达。结果：共识别出206种肠道微生物相关代谢物和1518个潜在靶点。网络分析预测了20个与SAE相关的关键靶点。PPI网络分析表明TNF、IL6、CXCL8、NFKB1和TLR4为中心节点。KEGG分析特别富集于Toll样受体、NOD样受体和NF-κB信号通路。综合筛选后保留了14种候选代谢物。在LPS处理的hCMEC/D3细胞中，大豆黄酮部分恢复了细胞活力、迁移和管形成能力，降低了IL-6和TNF-α水平，缓解了细胞内ROS积累，并与NFKB1、CXCL8和IL-6表达下调相关，同时伴随NF-κB p65和IκBα磷酸化减少。结论：本研究通过数据库支持的网络分析优先识别了与SAE相关的候选代谢物。初步体外验证提示大豆黄酮与炎症性内皮损伤相关表型的减轻有关，为进一步机制研究提供了基础。
